text:
maya: Heads-up: seeing a perf regression on fused-attn QKV-packed epilogue path after the last runtime change. p50 +15% on 4k sequences in our dedicated perf harness.
linus: ugh. which commit? can you paste the perf run id + raw numbers? :eyes: 
maya: run: perf/2026-03-10/epilogue-vs-master-224. Summary: master p50=42.3ms, current p50=48.7ms. p95 gap smaller but still present.
ci-bot: Perf run completed: https://ci.internal/runs/224 (summary attached) :white_check_mark:
maya: pasted the small tail of the benchmark log:
```
[bench] model=redwood-fused-attn q=packed epilogue=on seq=4096 bs=1
throughput: 210 tok/s -> 182 tok/s (-13.3%)
L2-misses: 12.3M -> 18.9M (+53%)
memcpy_bytes: 48MB -> 93MB (+93%)
```
linus: memcpy and L2 jumps smell like extra copies in the epilogue merge path. Did we enable taildrop/merge-window by default in the batcher change?
arjun: I instrumented the runtime and saw extra epilogue_merge calls when batcher splits into many small KV pages. Prefetching isn't overlapping because merge happens on CPU and forces sync.
zhen: repro notes? which hardware?
arjun: Ampere A100-p4. Repro steps: run fused-attn with packed QKV + paged-KV enabled + epilogue_merge_window=128. If you bump merge_window to 512 the behavior flips (less calls but bigger merges -> more memcpy per merge). Seems we traded off many small merges (cheap) for fewer large ones (expensive).
maya: interesting. For 4k seq, KV pages are ~64k each; merging 8 pages at once hits L2 foot-print hard. We probably need a heuristic: cap merge_bytes so per-merge working set fits L2.
linus: agree. Proposed heuristic: if seq > 2048 and batch_size_tokens > 16384 then set epilogue_merge_max_bytes = min( epilogue_merge_max_bytes, 256KB ). Otherwise keep default. Also prefer async memcpy on CUDA if available.
arjun: sketch of config we could add to runtime.yaml: 
```
batching:
  dynamic:
    seq_threshold: 2048
    token_ceiling: 16384
epilogue:
  merge_max_bytes: 262144   # 256KB
  allow_async_memcpy: true
```
zhen: can you attach perf counters for L2/A64 occupancy? I want to see cache miss ratio vs merge size.
arjun: dropped perf counters from the failing run:
```
PMC_L2_READS: 324_000_000
PMC_L2_MISSES: 18_900_000 -> miss_rate ~5.8%
DRAM_BYTES: +43MB
```
linus: 5.8% miss rate at that volume explains latency delta. If we limit per-merge footprint to 256KB we should cut misses by ~40-60% in microbench.
maya: ok can we do quick A/B? Arjun, can you run microbench with merge_max_bytes 256KB vs 1MB on the same hardware and post numbers? Also run with allow_async_memcpy toggled.
arjun: will run this afternoon and push a tiny patch to flip heuristic behind a feature-flag. I’ll also add a smoke test to perf harness to cover 2k-6k seq range.
ci-bot: Created issue #INF-492: "epilogue taildrop/merge heuristic causes memcpy/L2 thrash on large seq" and a PR stub to gate the new heuristic.
zhen: I’ll add a flamegraph capture step to the perf job so we can visualize memcpy hotspots. Quick note: adding more batching rarely helps if it increases per-request working set beyond L2. We should make batcher aware of L2-friendly merge sizes per-device.
linus: good point. maybe runtime should query device L2 size at startup and set merge_max_bytes = min( default, l2_size/4 ). That'd be robust across Ampere/Blackwell.
maya: love it. Action items: arjun run microbench + PR, zhen add flamegraph + regression test, linus add device L2 probe and config knob, maya follow up on CI job numbers.
arjun: assigned, ETA EOD tomorrow.
zhen: I’ll post flamegraphs here when ready.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup: Let’s keep the regression small and behind a flag until we validate.
linus: if anyone hits this on Dedicated clusters, create a support note and we can flip the flag runtime-side for affected customers.
ci-bot: linked PR: https://ci.internal/prs/734 :rocket:
